notes: Version 2, corrected after prescore review -- see charter-teaching-note.md for what changed and why. Magnitude source: POS order timestamps plus the pickup-counter handoff tally, 15 mornings sampled across Q2 2026, n = 412 orders.

problem_statement.what: Espresso-drink orders take too long from register to handoff during the weekday morning peak, producing walk-aways, comped drinks, remakes, and peak-end overtime.
problem_statement.where: Campus coffee bar, front counter and espresso station.
problem_statement.when: Weekday mornings, 7:00-10:00 peak; observed throughout Q2 2026.

goal.statement: Reduce average order-to-handoff time during the weekday 7:00-10:00 peak from 8.4 minutes to 5.0 minutes by October 31, 2026.
consequential_metrics: Barista labor hours per morning shift

scope.in_scope: Espresso-drink orders placed at the register during the weekday 7:00-10:00 peak: order-taking, drink preparation, and handoff at the campus coffee bar.
scope.out_scope: Food orders, drip-only orders, mobile pre-orders, weekend service, the library cart, menu changes, and pricing.

process_owner.name: Priya Shah
process_owner.role: Morning shift lead -- runs the order-to-handoff process daily

business_impact.basis: COPQ calculator Q2 2026 total ($4,021) x 4 -- Q2 actuals x 4

risks.risk: Fall semester starts late August and shifts morning demand, so before/after comparisons could be confounded
risks.mitigation: Record daily order counts as a stratification factor and compare like-for-like weeks

risks.risk: Student-barista turnover mid-project loses the trained morning crew
risks.mitigation: Cross-train a second regular on the espresso station; log staffing changes in the project record
